Pooled quantile regression with a child-level cluster bootstrap

Source: R/quant-rq.R
wgh_rq.Rd

Fits quantile regressions at several quantiles on one fixed design matrix (so every bootstrap replicate uses the same spline basis), resamples children with all their visits to get honest uncertainty for repeated measures, and reports the exposure slope at stated ages by contrast. This is the rq_pipeline() of Book 2 Chapter 4 made general, and the engine behind the growth inequality study's dispersion analysis.

Usage

wgh_rq(
  x,
  formula,
  taus = wgh_taus("headline"),
  exposure = "baz",
  anchor_ages = c(6, 9, 12, 15),
  fixed = list(),
  B = wgh_opt("B"),
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

x

Growth data (one sex at a time, or include sex in the formula).

formula

Model formula, for example haz ~ splines::ns(age, knots = c(8, 11, 14), Boundary.knots = c(5, 18)) * baz + site.

taus

Quantiles (rounded with wgh_taus()).

exposure

Exposure whose slope is reported.

anchor_ages

Ages at which slopes are reported.

fixed

Values for other model variables in the slope contrasts (default: first factor level and the mean of numeric variables).

B

Bootstrap replicates (default from the run mode). 0 skips the bootstrap.

seed

Random seed.

Value

An object of class wgh_rq with coefs (one column per quantile), boot (array of bootstrap coefficient matrices), slopes (estimates, bootstrap SE and percentile intervals) and the design.

Details

Write spline knots into the formula (for example splines::ns(age, knots = c(8, 11, 14), Boundary.knots = c(5, 18))) so the basis does not change between replicates.

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- growdat[growdat$sex == "Female" & growdat$age >= 5, ]
f <- haz ~ splines::ns(age, knots = c(8, 11, 14), Boundary.knots = c(5, 18.5)) * baz
fit <- wgh_rq(d, f, taus = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), anchor_ages = c(6, 9, 12, 15), B = 30)
fit
